title: POC weekly sync - throughput optimization
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput numbers from last benchmark, discuss continuous batching tweaks, adjust concurrency and queueing targets, and agree next steps for a 2-week scale test. Customer expressed latency vs cost tradeoffs and asked for a small canary on Dedicated. Action items: Redwood to share updated benchmark sheet and suggested autoscaler settings; Novapay to provide production traffic histogram and confirm security checklist items.
next_steps: Redwood to send updated benchmark spreadsheet with per-batch latency/cost breakdown (by 2026-03-15)
Novapay to share 7-day production request histogram and 95th p95 latency target (by 2026-03-16)
Schedule 2-hour canary run on Dedicated for 2026-03-24
SE to propose autoscaler / queue size config in Confluence doc
action_items: Priya Nair: run a micro-benchmark varying target_concurrency 4/8/16 and send results (due 2026-03-15)
Jordan Patel: update pricing / cost model for Dedicated canary and share via spreadsheet (due 2026-03-16)
Carlos Mendes: export 7-day traffic histogram and share S3 link (due 2026-03-16)
Asha Rao: confirm SOC2 logs retention requirement and KMS key policy (due 2026-03-18)
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for jumping on, this is Jordan from Redwood. quick rollcall?
00:06 Carlos Mendes: Hey Jordan, Carlos here.
00:08 Asha Rao: Asha, hi.
:10 Liam Chen: Liam, SRE.
00:12 Jordan Patel: Great, Priya from our SE team is on too. The goal for today is to go over last week's throughput runs and tune continuous batching / concurrency so the POC hits Novapay's 500 req/s plateau without breaking p95.
00:28 Priya Nair: Yeah I ran the micro-benchmarks overnight, sent a raw sheet, but it's a bit noisy, sorry about the naming on some tabs.
00:36 Carlos Mendes: I saw it, thanks. initial look saw big variance at high concurrency, p95 spiked.
00:41 Priya Nair: Correct, when target_concurrency goes above 8 we see queueing in the request path that increases p95 because of tail queuing; continuous batching helps but youhit diminishing returns if batch wait time grows.
00:55 Carlos Mendes: Quick context: our prod traffic has lots of short requests, median tokens 24, but spikes to 128 tokens during batch payouts. Our hard target is p95 < 320ms for auth flows, but for other flows 500ms is ok.
01:11 Jordan Patel: helpful, thanks. So the tuning levers we've been testing are: batch_max_tokens, batch_wait_ms, target_concurrency, and autoscaler backpressure settings. Also we tried KV cache warmup which helped repeated keys.
01:26 Priya Nair: Right, note on KV cache: the first-pass had some warmup misses because our synthetic load didn't preserve conversation affinity. In real traffic with sticky session ids the KV hit rate should be much higher which reduces compute per request.
01:40 Asha Rao: For Dedicated we're looking at GPU pool sizing and whether to pin 4 clients per GPU or ramp to 8. Cost team wants to avoid oversubscribe.
01:50 Liam Chen: Also want to avoid contention on the host CPU when many small batches are formed — saw CPU steal on the instance in the last run.
02:00 Priya Nair: CPU overhead is from the pre- and post-processing threads, and the queue manager. We suggested using smaller batch sizes but higher concurrency to keep GPU busy — it's a tradeoff.
02:11 Carlos Mendes: Can you summarize the numbers from your overnight runs? what's the best config you found?
02:18 Priya Nair: Sure. top config: target_concurrency=8, batch_wait_ms=12, batch_max_tokens=2048. That gave sustained 520 req/s with median latency ~170ms and p95 ~310ms on our 4xA100 equivalent nodes. At concurrency 16, throughput rose to 720 req/s but p95 jumped to ~520ms because queueing delay dominated.
02:40 Jordan Patel: note those numbers were on our internal test harness with CPU limits slightly higher; your infra might see different p95s, so we should run a canary with your real traffic histogram.
02:51 Carlos Mendes: That makes sense. The 310ms p95 is close to our 320ms target; but worried about the spike windows.
02:59 Priya Nair: We can use a hybrid policy: target_concurrency=8 as baseline, and burst slots up to 12 with a short token-leaky queue for smoothing. Essentially prioritize latency-critical routes.
03:11 Liam Chen: How do you implement the burst policy? Is that in the Redwood autoscaler?
03:14 Priya Nair: It's a routing + autoscaler config. We set per-route concurrency caps and a queue size. The autoscaler will add more GPUs if queue length sustained beyond threshold. We also add a fallback to a cheaper quantized model for non-critical traffic.
03:29 Asha Rao: Quantized model — have you validated quality delta? procurement needs to know risk.
03:33 Jordan Patel: We did a blind eval last month; quality drop was negligible for our prompt family, but we'll share the evaluation doc. Carlos, we can mark non-auth flows to go to the quantized variant.
03:45 Carlos Mendes: Good. On security: we need to confirm KMS and audit log retention for Dedicated. Any blockers?
03:51 Jordan Patel: No blockers. We support customer-managed keys (bring your own KMS) and we can stream audit logs to your S3 or syslog. Will include details in the security pack.
04:02 Priya Nair: Back to queueing: one thing we saw is that when multiple very large token requests hit, KV cache misses plus large decode times cause the scheduler to hold small requests behind big ones. We recommend request partitioning by expected token length or using a prioritized queue so small auth requests skip ahead.
04:20 Liam Chen: Prioritized queue sounds attractive. How hard is that to configure?
04:24 Priya Nair: It's a toggle plus a per-route priority tag in the routing policy, we can demo in the next session.
04:31 Carlos Mendes: For observability, can you push per-token latency histogram and per-batch size distribution to our Grafana?
04:36 Jordan Patel: Yes, we can forward metrics; we'll map metric names. Priya will add recommended dashboards to the Confluence doc.
04:45 Priya Nair: Action items: I'll run additional micro-benchmarks varying concurrency 4/8/12 and test prioritized queue vs FIFO. Also I'll capture CPU wait stats and per-batch latency breakdown.
04:56 Carlos Mendes: We'll export a 7-day histogram of request sizes and a list of routes that are latency-critical.
05:03 Asha Rao: on the Dedicated canary, cost team needs estimate — Jordan can you share the pricing?
05:08 Jordan Patel: Yes I'll send a cost model; the canary for 2 hours on a 2-node Dedicated pool should be small; I'll put numbers in spreadsheet.
05:18 Liam Chen: One more thing: in previous runs there's a tail related to context window resets. Are you doing KV cache eviction policy tuning?
05:25 Priya Nair: We are. We tuned the KV cache LRU windows; we can increase kept keys for the canary to reduce misses. That will increase memory but should help p95.
05:36 Carlos Mendes: Sounds good. If the canary looks good we may go to a 1-week scale test.
05:41 Jordan Patel: Great. Recap of next steps: Redwood to share updated benchmark spreadsheet and autoscaler recommendations by Monday (2026-03-15). Novapay to share traffic histogram and list of critical routes by Tuesday. SE and Novapay to schedule Dedicated canary for 2026-03-24.
05:58 Asha Rao: Thanks, bye.
06:00 Jordan Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
